title: Quick Accent doesn't activate anymore after pressing 1, after pressing another character e.g. 2

judgment.rationale: The report gives a specific sequential-key failure on PowerToys 0.101.2362.0, including loss of further Quick Accent use until the feature is restarted. Current owner code processes numeric keys only when the selected accent language has a mapping and normally clears the active owner on key-up, so the cause is unconfirmed. A low-confidence, testable state-cleanup hypothesis is suitable for a reproduction-first candidate, not an implementation-ready design.
evidence: The reporter says 2 plus left/right opens accent choices, but 1 plus left/right does not show the picker and leaves Quick Accent unusable until manually toggled off and on.
The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.101.2362, Windows 10 IoT Enterprise build 19045.7807, system installation, and not running as administrator.

The sole comment is automated triage at 2026-10-15T01:47:20Z; it says the attached archive could not be analyzed as an invalid archive and that public reproduction steps are sufficient. Its contents were not accessed or copied.
Current upstream PowerAccent source has language-dependent numeric mappings and explicit owner/toolbar reset logic; it does not establish which transition fails.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the paired maintainer reproduction with a language that maps both 1 and 2, then trace key-down/key-up and cancel/hide transitions before approving any implementation-grade design.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing upstream fix or MuyuanMS/PowerToys issue, PR, or branch trace was found for #51311. A PowerAccent code change is applicable if reproduction confirms the reported loss of input response; the specific failing transition remains unverified.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover Quick Accent after a failed numeric-key gesture
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reported 2-to-1 sequence followed by feature-wide loss of response is consistent with an incomplete numeric owner gesture leaving KeyboardListener state stale. This is only a hypothesis: current OnKeyUp clears letterPressed and hides the toolbar on a normal active-owner release, and the issue does not state the selected Quick Accent language.
plan: Reproduce on the reported Windows 10 build; record the selected Quick Accent language and activation mode and confirm that both numeric keys have mappings.

Trace KeyboardListener::OnKeyDown and KeyboardListener::OnKeyUp through 2, navigation, release, 1, navigation, and release; verify that owner cleanup and cancel/hide callbacks clear m_toolbarVisible and letterPressed.

Only if the trace confirms stale state, correct the specific release/cancel transition so an unsuccessful second digit gesture cannot disable later gestures, while preserving valid selection and normal key forwarding.
Add a regression for a successful 2 gesture followed by a failed 1 gesture and then another numeric and alphabetic gesture, plus a no-mapping control.
verification: Run focused PowerAccent unit coverage and a PowerAccent end-to-end test on Windows 10 build 19045 with the reproducing language and activation settings.
Verify configured 1 and 2 mappings open and navigate the picker, and a failed 1 attempt does not prevent later Quick Accent activation or alter unrelated key input.

confidence.rationale: The user-visible failure is specific, but selected accent language is unknown and current source has a normal key-up cleanup path; reproduction and state tracing could disprove the hypothesis cheaply.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent reportedly stops opening after a successful digit-key picker sequence is followed by 1, and remains unresponsive until manually restarted.
known_information: PowerToys 0.101.2362 on Windows 10 IoT Enterprise build 19045.7807; system installation; not running as administrator; English (US) keyboard locale.
Reported sequence uses 2 with left/right to choose accents, then 1 with left/right; the latter shows no picker and Quick Accent must be toggled off/on to recover.
The sole automated triage comment says the linked archive was rejected as an invalid archive format and considers the public reproduction steps sufficient. Diagnostic contents were not accessed.
The selected Quick Accent language/character set is not stated; Windows keyboard locale does not establish that setting.
inferences: A stuck owner/toolbar gesture state is one plausible explanation for feature-wide loss of response, but current source has explicit normal key-up cleanup and no failing transition has been observed.
Whether the selected language maps both digits 1 and 2 affects whether both gestures should open a picker and which activation branch is exercised.
issue_context.analysis: The report is concrete enough for maintainer reproduction without requesting another archive. The smallest useful next step is to reproduce with a language that maps both digits, then determine whether the owner-release/cancel lifecycle leaves state behind. Keep the confidence red and do not treat the hypothesis as an implementation-ready design.
initial_investigation: At upstream source head 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a, PowerAccent.Common/CharacterMappings.cs contains numeric mappings for language-specific entries including Special and Pinyin; the configured language is material.

PowerAccentKeyboardService/KeyboardListener.cpp::OnKeyDown gates a new owner gesture on the configured language mapping and captures activation settings. OnKeyUp clears the active owner and, for a visible toolbar, calls the hide callback and clears visible state. This is counterevidence to assuming an unconditional stale-state bug and narrows the required trace.
No direct linked issue or fix was cited in the live discussion. Searched MuyuanMS/PowerToys issues, PRs, and branch names; no #51311 trace was found.

information_gaps.information: The Quick Accent selected language/character set and activation mode used for the 2-to-1 sequence.
information_gaps.why_needed: Numeric accent mappings vary by selected language, while the issue states only the Windows keyboard locale; this confirms whether both digits should open a picker and which activation branch is involved.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Read the Quick Accent settings page during reproduction; no full settings export or diagnostic archive is needed.

reproduce.version_requirement: First use PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 if available, then verify on the current stable build; target Windows 10 IoT Enterprise build 19045.7807 when available.
prerequisites: Enable Quick Accent and use a configured language with mappings for both 1 and 2 (for example, the Special or Pinyin mappings in current upstream source).
Use the reported left/right activation behavior and record the Quick Accent activation setting.
Release all keys between the two digit sequences.
steps: Start PowerToys and confirm the selected Quick Accent language and activation setting.
Hold 2 and press left/right to open and navigate the choices; release all keys and verify Quick Accent returns to idle.
Hold 1 and press left/right; observe whether the picker appears and navigation works.
If the second sequence fails, test whether a later mapped digit and an alphabetic key can still open Quick Accent before toggling the feature.
Record KeyboardListener key-down/key-up and show/cancel/hide state transitions; do not capture or publish unrelated user diagnostics.
reproduce.expected_result: Each configured numeric key opens and navigates its accent choices. A failed second gesture must not leave Quick Accent unusable or prevent a later valid gesture.
setup_requirements: Record the selected Quick Accent language and activation mode; do not infer the feature mapping from the English (US) Windows keyboard locale.
Run on the reported Windows build when possible, then compare with the current stable build.
